findings.observation: New RPA paper confirmed real and indexed: Netherton TJ et al., 'Artificial Intelligence-Powered Radiotherapy for Resource-Limited Settings: Advancing Cervical and Prostate Cancer Treatment Planning With the Radiation Planning Assistant', JCO Global Oncology 2026;12(7):e2500702, DOI 10.1200/GO-25-00702, PMID 42424567, verified present in Europe PMC (hitCount=1, firstPublicationDate 2026-07-09).
findings.suggestedFix: Add this DOI to the RPA evidence array as a new multi-institutional peer-reviewed publication (prostate >1,000 plans, cervical 110 plans, EMBRACE II-aligned, nnU-Net auto-contouring + knowledge-based planning); it strengthens — but on its own does not elevate beyond — the existing E2 rating since it is MD Anderson-led (not yet independently externally authored in the same sense as Court 2024).

findings.observation: The stored evidenceRigorNotes narrative predates this 2026-07-09 publication and does not yet mention it; the catalogue's most recent RPA sweep language stops at Lloyd 2026/Kavuma 2025 context.
findings.suggestedFix: Append a dated note referencing GO-25-00702 and re-confirm whether E2 should be retained or whether this new prospective/validated expansion to cervical+prostate workflows with EMBRACE II alignment should be considered toward E3 criteria (would still require independent/non-MDACC confirmation).

limitations: Did not exhaustively re-verify every one of the 9 evidence[] DOIs individually (relied on the existing 2026-09-23 HAIR cross-check annotations); evaluationData.studyDesign/results text may also need rewording once the source citation is fixed.

findings.observation: Verified three distinct Manteia FDA clearances exist: MOZI TPS (K223724, full treatment-planning system — dose calculation, Monte Carlo, plan optimization, photon EBRT); AccuContour 4.0 (K251351, pure segmentation: 'used by the radiation oncology department to segment CT images'); and ARTAssistant (K250780, NOT in inventory — an adaptive-RT image-processing assistant whose three functions are (1) rigid/deformable registration, (2) sCT GENERATION from CBCT or MR, and (3) assisted/manual OAR contouring). ARTAssistant's predicate is AccuContour (K221706) and references MRI Planner (K211841) and RayStation (K220141), confirming it is a separate product line, not a MOZI/AccuContour version bump.
findings.suggestedFix: No change needed to MOZI TPS entry itself; this finding supports NOT conflating MOZI (planning), AccuContour (segmentation), and ARTAssistant (registration+sCT generation+contour-assist) as the same product, per instruction not to conflate sCT generation and sCT segmentation — ARTAssistant performs sCT generation (image conversion) as a separate function from its (non-AI-specified) contouring tool, and is functionally distinct from AccuContour's segmentation-only clearance.

limitations: AccuContour 4.0 (K251351) is already correctly tracked inside the existing 'AccuContour' auto-contouring inventory entry (lines ~6513 of inventory.json), so it is NOT a missing/duplicate candidate — confirmed to avoid false-positive duplication flag.

findings.observation: SeeTreat ART.1 / ART.1-US (K253078, cleared 2026-05-14, product code MUJ) performs adaptive-RT image registration, synthetic CT generation, contour propagation and dose calculation for daily CBCT-based replan decision support. The vendor explicitly describes it as built on 'purpose-built image registration and dose calculation algorithms' without claiming a deep-learning/AI basis in its public materials (product page, FDA RWE summary); no AI/ML terminology is used in the Indications for Use or device description.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat as OUT OF SCOPE for this AI-in-RT catalogue (classical/non-AI algorithmic adaptive-RT QA tool) unless the manufacturer discloses a deep-learning component in the 510(k) summary; do not add as a new AI product candidate. Confirmed distinct from, and not a duplicate of, any existing Performance Monitor entry (it computes dose/contours itself rather than merely monitoring another AI's outputs).
